surfaces.part: top cap / header band of the sign

answer.evidence: The signboard is a tall standing slab. Rows 1-4 form a crimson band with a white highlight on row 1. Row 5 is a darker line (L=38 against L=59 above), which works as a front-edge line. Row 6 is the darkest row (L=17) and acts as eave shadow. Below that, rows 7-28 are the vertical lettered panel and rows 29-30 are a grey base, giving about 24 rows of front face. The top band is ambiguous because it could be a front-facing header, but it has an edge line and shadow, so I count it as a top surface of about 5 rows. No side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small vertical sign with a dark red-brown outline that leans tinted, matching its maroon body. The measured near-neutral share of dark edge pixels is 0%, so this is not a black sticker line. It has a lighter red edge band, a mid red body and light lettering. That gives about 4 steps, a little under the references' roughly 5 to 6. Visible tones per tile are 7, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, lower than bus-shelter-a's 9%, because the lettering and border break up the body. It is simpler than kiosk-a and vending-a, but it sits at or above the bus-shelter-a level that is already shipped in this chipset. I would not call it thinner or more sticker-like than that reference, so it passes, though not by a wide margin.

surfaces.part: top header band of the sign
sign board face with Korean lettering

answer.evidence: This is a tall, flat signboard drawn face-on. Rows 1-4 are a crimson header band that is the same width as the board (14 px). It has only a small highlight at row 1 and the width profile does not widen and narrow like an ellipse. Row 5 is a slightly darker line and row 6 is the dark outline, so the band reads as a front-facing cap, not a horizontal surface seen from above. Below it, rows 7-29 are the board face with the cream lettering and a dark right-hand edge strip, and row 30 is a grey base. The silhouette is a plain upright rectangle (10 px at row 0, 12 px at rows 1-2, 14 px from row 3). No receding side face and no top plane are drawn, so it reads as front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow red sign slab with a tinted dark-red edge, a lighter highlight strip down the left side, and pale lettering. It shows 7 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) but below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0% (bus-shelter-a: 9%), because the lettering and highlight break up the body. The edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans dark red-brown rather than black, matching the references. The body ramp is shallow, about 4 steps (highlight, base red, dark red, edge) against roughly 5 in the references, and it has little grain. It is a simple single-purpose sign, so this is acceptable. It is at least as dense as the plainest shipped piece (bus-shelter-a) and is not a black-outlined sticker.

Row 5 is a darker band and row 6 is a near-black outline separating it from the panel, but the header is the same width as the panel and has no sloped plane. I read it as a front-facing cap rather than a top surface. The grey base (rows 29-31) is also a face-on strip. Nothing shows a horizontal surface seen from above, and there is no receding side face, so the object reads as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a dark red vertical sign with a lighter red edge and cream lettering. The body shows about 4 red steps (highlight rim, mid, dark, deep), plus the cream text. The outline is a deep red-brown tinted version of the body, not black, and 0% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral, which matches all three references. It has 7 visible tones per tile against 6 for bus-shelter-a, 12 for kiosk-a and 20 for vending-a. Near-flat coverage is 0%, against 9% for bus-shelter-a, so there are no large flat fills. It is a simple single-tile prop and sits slightly below kiosk-a and vending-a in richness. It is at least as rich as bus-shelter-a and would not look thinner or more sticker-like beside the shipped modern_city art.
